title: Взрыв на кухне и руины правды  (Kitchen Explosion and the Ruins of Truth)

segments.t: The confrontation spills into the kitchen as Vika brings up the rumor about Chef Barinov reciting poetry to Louis, causing Viktor Petrovich's anger-management technique to implode completely. Watching the chaos, Max reflects on how every reckless act eventually leaves behind only ruins.
Ну вы, конечно, друг друга стоите.
Вы же себе позволяете, Витя, кто это?
Каждый необдуманный поступок в нашей жизни –.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Ну вы, конечно, друг друга стоите.
'Well, you two certainly deserve each other.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'are standing'.
'Just listen to him talk.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'listen'. Nastya answers right away.
'And what about yourself?' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'himself' in spoken Russian.
Вы же себе позволяете, Витя, кто это?
'What are you allowing yourself to do, Vitya, who is this?' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'this' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'What nonsense are you all spouting in here?' Vika raises the pitch on 'bring' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Nastya answers right away.
'Why on earth do you need Louis?' The grammar packs 'what for' and 'Louis' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'I am going to explain everything right now.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'any minute', while 'I will explain' completes the thought.
'Why does all of this remind me of something?' Notice how Russian expresses 'somehow' and 'reminds of' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Nastya answers right away.
'I am going to explain it to all of you right now!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'I will explain'.
'You are not even trying to change.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'to try' to negate the statement.
Каждый необдуманный поступок в нашей жизни –.
'Every reckless action in our lives is a mine.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'every' and finishing on 'life'. Nastya answers right away.
'Looking back, we see nothing but ruins.' The meaning hinges on 'we' working together with 'ruin' in spoken Russian.
'You know what?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'know', while 'what' completes the thought. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Ну вы, конечно, друг друга стоите.
Вы же себе позволяете, Витя, кто это?
Каждый необдуманный поступок в нашей жизни –.
